text:
incident-bot: SLO Burn Rate Alert: /slo/service/latency 15m window burned > 120% (alerting policy: burnrate-multiwindow-prod). paging: paged jamal.

jamal: saw the bot — is this a real customer impact or a transient burst?

maria: looks like ~10% of p50 requests spiked for the last 8m, mostly in eu-west-1. frontend dashboards show a short GC/redis blip on a couple of hosts. not wide but enough to push burn.

alex: can we avoid paging for these short spikes? right now policy pages at 2x baseline in any 5m window. maybe tune to multi-window logic.

jamal: on it. declaring incident level: advisory. I'm oncall and will triage. li, can you pull the 1m-5m latency tails?

li: pulling now. dashboards: https://graf/redwood/d/latency/prod?var=service

ops-bot: Created incident INC-2026-2347 and runbook pinned: https://wiki/redwood/oncall/runbooks/slo-burn

maria: quick customer check — I scanned support queue, no direct customer complaints yet. a handful of retries at 503 from a mobile SDK, likely correlated.

jamal: ok — probably limited customer impact but alert noise is high. propose: 1) temporary paging suppression for 10m while we mitigate 2) change burn-rate alert config to require crossing threshold in two windows (5m and 15m) before paging 3) create new dashboard panel to surface host-level KV cache evictions.

priya: +1 to multi-window. we've been bitten by 1-window flapping. also recommend an emergency guard: page only if global burn > 150% OR localized region > 200% for > 10m.

alex: agree. here's a minimal rule tweak we can push fast (Prometheus alert manager style):

```yaml
- alert: SLOBurn_MultiWindow
  expr: (burn_5m > 2 and burn_15m > 1.2) or (region_burn_10m > 2)
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "SLO burn multiwindow
"
```

jamal: thanks. I'm going to mute paging for the current alert so oncall rotation isn't interrupted while we test. ops-bot, mute rule burnrate-multiwindow-prod for 10m.

ops-bot: Done. mute applied to policy burnrate-multiwindow-prod for 10m by jamal.

li: host list for affected requests: host-12, host-19, host-21. KV cache miss rate on host-19 is 87% for the last 10m. likely OOM/restart or eviction storm.

maria: I can push a small restart to host-19 and drain it, but that will cause a short routing churn. recommend cordon + restart on low-traffic buckets.

jamal: go ahead maria. alex/priya — after we stabilize let's push the alert rule change to staging and run for 24h. then propose to SLO committee for permanent adoption. also add a dashboard card and an alert on KV eviction rate with a non-paging severity.

alex: noted. followups: #1 update alert config PR with multiwindow expr and guardrails, #2 create dashboard PR with KV eviction panel + region breakdown, #3 add runbook section for paging criteria and multi-window rationale.

maria: restart started on host-19. monitoring shows latency coming down within 90s.

li: confirmed — p50/p95 normalized. burn rate trending down.

jamal: thanks all. I'll close incident when the next 20m looks stable. provisional action items posted in the incident ticket.

incident-bot: INC-2026-2347 updated: status=monitoring, assignee=jamal, timeline added.

priya: one more thought — for long-term, consider adding smoothing to burn rate calc (exponential moving average) to avoid flapping from short bursts. worth a follow-up RFC.

alex: agreed. I'll draft a short RFC and include cost/alert-noise tradeoffs.

jamal: closing note: if anyone sees repeated 1-5m burn spikes next week, escalate to paging immediately. otherwise let's test the multi-window rule in staging. thanks :thumbsup:
